newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan hails businessman's shoe donation to Haiti.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan hails businessman's shoe donation to Haiti.

text.p: Taiwan, trying to break out of diplomatic isolation imposed by rival China, hailed on Wednesday the donation of 25,000 pairs of shoes to Haiti by a Taiwanese businessman as a diplomatic accomplishment.

Chen Yo-liang, a Taiwanese businessman living in the United States, donated the shoes this week to the Haitian government for distribution among the poor children in the Caribbean state -- one of only 30 nations that have formal diplomatic ties with Taipei.

"Mr Chen's act of 'delivering coal in snow' not only has won the gratitude and friendship of the Haitian people, it also added a new page to the diplomatic achievement of our people," Taiwan's foreign ministry said in a statement.
Taiwan has stepped up efforts to court its allies after South Africa, its largest diplomatic partner, announced in November it would switch recognition from Taipei to Beijing by the end of 1997.

China and Taiwan separated after a civil war ended in 1949, but Beijing still regards the island as a renegade province not entitled to diplomatic relations, and refuses to have formal ties with countries that recognise Taipei.
